title: Types of Volcano
welcome_lead: Not all volcanoes are the same. Compare steep composite cones with gentle shield volcanoes — and meet the deadly pyroclastic flow.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on composite vs shield volcanoes and pyroclastic flows.
final_note: Excellent! You can now compare volcano types.

walkthroughs.body_html: Composite (stratovolcanoes) have steep sides built from many eruptions. Their thick lava traps gas, causing explosive eruptions. Vesuvius and Mount Fuji are examples.
Shield volcanoes have wide, gentle slopes. Their runny lava flows far before cooling. Mauna Loa in Hawaii is the largest active example.
A pyroclastic flow is a deadly mix of hot gas, ash and rock that races down a volcano at up to 700 km/h. It killed thousands in Pompeii (79 CE).

mcqs.q: How do rivers transport their load?
options: Rivers can only transport material when they are in flood.
By traction (rolling large stones along the bed), saltation (bouncing smaller pebbles), suspension (carrying fine sediment in the flow) and solution (dissolved minerals).
Rivers transport everything by pushing it along the bottom.
The ITCZ is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

mcqs.q: What is the ITCZ and why does it bring rain?
options: Rivers can only transport material when they are in flood.
The ITCZ is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
The Intertropical Convergence Zone is where trade winds from both hemispheres converge near the equator, forcing air to rise, cool and produce heavy convectional rainfall.
The ITCZ is a fixed band of permanent storms at the equator.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between random, stratified and systematic sampling?
options: Random: every member has equal chance of selection. Systematic: pick every nth item. Stratified: divide the population into groups and sample proportionally from each — ensures subgroup representation.
Stratified sampling means picking samples from different strata of rock.
Rivers can only transport material when they are in flood.
All three sampling methods produce the same results.
